::: {.block title="1. Does hyperspectral help?"}
We trained the same model on the same BGC-Argo profiles with three inputs:
OLCI's 11 bands, the 11 PACE bands nearest them, and all 172 PACE bands. PACE-172
scores higher than OLCI-11 in every repeat, but only by 0.01–0.03 in R², and
most of that gain already comes from PACE's 11 bands, which points to the sensor
rather than the extra bands. Training each sensor on all of its own matchups
helps about as much. For OOI, no input predicts below the surface.

| Input | Trained on | 0–10 m | 50–60 m | 100–110 m | Integrated |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| OLCI-11 | Both | 0.75 | 0.57 | 0.39 | 0.28 |
| PACE-11 | Both | 0.75 | 0.59 | 0.40 | 0.31 |
| PACE-172 | Both | 0.76 | 0.60 | 0.41 | 0.32 |
| OLCI-11 | All, 2.5× | 0.76 | 0.58 | 0.40 | 0.31 |
| PACE-172 | All, 1.9× | **0.76** | **0.61** | **0.42** | **0.33** |

: R² of log10 Chl *a* for BGC-Argo, scored on the same held-out profiles (space-time split, mean of 3 repeats). Trained on profiles with both sensors, or on all of that sensor's matchups. {#tbl-hyperspectral}
:::
